candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: understand expected medication actions/outcomes, provide medication education, monitor therapeutic effects, and safely manage prescribed drug therapy.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — expected action of calcitriol in renal metabolic bone disease
candidate.educational_objective: Explain the role of calcitriol in chronic renal dialysis as active vitamin D therapy that enhances calcium absorption and may reduce elevated PTH in renal metabolic bone disease.

options.A: Calcitriol is the active form of vitamin D; in dialysis patients it enhances calcium absorption and may reduce elevated parathyroid hormone levels as part of management of renal metabolic bone disease.
options.B: Calcitriol lowers serum phosphorus by remaining in the gastrointestinal tract and binding dietary phosphate before absorption.
options.C: Calcitriol directly increases parathyroid hormone secretion so that serum calcium can be lowered during dialysis.
options.D: Calcitriol works primarily as a loop diuretic that increases urinary calcium and phosphorus excretion.

candidate.rationale: Current calcitriol prescribing information identifies calcitriol as the active form of vitamin D and indicates it for management of hypocalcemia and resultant metabolic bone disease in patients undergoing chronic renal dialysis. In these patients, calcitriol enhances calcium absorption and may reduce elevated parathyroid hormone levels. It is not a gastrointestinal phosphate binder, does not increase PTH as its intended effect, and is not a loop diuretic. Therefore, A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports calcitriol use in chronic renal dialysis for hypocalcemia/metabolic bone disease, including enhanced calcium absorption and possible reduction of elevated PTH.
candidate.source_locator: Indications and Usage → Dialysis Patients: calcitriol is indicated in management of hypocalcemia and resultant metabolic bone disease in patients undergoing chronic renal dialysis; administration enhances calcium absorption, reduces serum alkaline phosphatase, and may reduce elevated PTH and manifestations of renal osteodystrophy. Description/clinical pharmacology identifies calcitriol as the active form/metabolite of vitamin D.
candidate.source_organization: National Library of Medicine / U.S. Food and Drug Administration labeling via DailyMed
candidate.stem: A client undergoing chronic renal dialysis is prescribed calcitriol for hypocalcemia and renal metabolic bone disease. Which explanation by the nurse is most accurate?
